title: Huntik Trading Card Game
summary:
The Huntik Trading Card Game (TCG) is a two-player trading card game based upon the Huntik: Secrets & Seekers television series. The cards, which are collected randomly by players and assembled into 40-card decks, represent various Seekers, Titans, and spells from the world of Huntik. The game was published by Upper Deck Entertainment in Europe and the United States and launched on February 17, 2009 with the release of the Secrets and Seekers Starter Deck and its supporting boosters. It was accompanied by the Huntik TCG Tutorial, a special minisode featuring Lok Lambert, Dante Vale and Cherit playing and explaining the game. Each Huntik booster pack contains 9 cards, including a foil rare in every pack while 1 in every 3 contains a password card that could unlock exclusive content on Huntik.com.

The Huntik TCG is notable for its integration into the Huntik television series, with the visual design of the cards closely resembling the informational cards displayed on the Holotome in the series, and the Titan cards functioning as an in-universe extension of the Holotome's Titan profile system, translating on-screen information into a playable format. In addition, the TCG expands on Huntik's lore, introducing many new original Seekers, Titans and Spells, and revealing new information and backstories for elements seen in the show.

sections.heading: Development and Launch
sections.wikitext:
Big Bocca's development of the Huntik TCG began in 2008, designing its mechanics alongside the production of the ''Huntik'' television series, ensuring close thematic integration between the cards and the show’s characters, Titans, locations, and story arcs. It was particularly notable for expanding on Huntik's mythology, introducing many original [[Seekers]], [[Titans]] and [[Spells]] and providing new information and backstories for elements in the show. Ahead of the TCG's official launch, Sneak Preview events were organised by Upper Deck where exclusive [[TCG:Pre-Release Cards|Pre-Release Cards]] were given out. The first set, [[TCG:Secrets and Seekers|Secrets and Seekers]], was released on February 17, 2009. It introduced the core gameplay mechanics, and featured characters and Titan from first half of the [[Season 1|first season]] of the show and consisted of the [[TCG:Starter Deck|Starter Deck]] and booster packs. A special [[Huntik TCG Tutorial]] was also released featuring [[Lok Lambert]], [[Dante Vale]] and [[Cherit]] playing the game and explaining the gameplay to the viewers. 

Later in 2009, Upper Deck released two expansion sets: [[TCG:Legendary Saga|Legendary Saga]] (June 2009), which introduced the four Legendary Titans and added higher-rarity, more powerful hero cards, and [[TCG:Omens and Legacies|Omens and Legacies]] (October 2009), which expanded the game’s narrative scope by introducing new factions such as the [[Blood Spiral|Blood Spirals]] and incorporating elements from later parts of the series’ storyline. In addition to standard expansions, Upper Deck released [[TCG:Promotional Cards|Promotional Cards]] through organized play programs such as Seeker League events and tournaments, as well as special collector products like the [[TCG:Huntik Holotome Tin|Huntik Holotome Tin]], which bundled booster packs with exclusive cards.

sections.heading: Planned Expansions and Cancellation
sections.wikitext: Upper Deck had planned to continue supporting the Huntik TCG with additional expansions in 2010, notably the fourth set, [[TCG:Labyrinth of Doom|Labyrinth of Doom]], which was intended to further develop the game’s mechanics and story content and feature characters from the show's [[Season 2|second season]]. However, this set was never released due to Upper Deck Entertainment filing for bankruptcy amid legal disputes and financial difficulties. As a result, production and organized support for several of the company’s trading card games including the Huntik TCG were discontinued. Planned expansions were cancelled, and the game ceased receiving official updates, tournament support, or new releases.

sections.heading: Gameplay
sections.wikitext:
*Each player assembles a 40-card deck, containing Seekers, Titans, and actions such as [[magic|spells]] from either the good factions ([[Huntik Foundation]] and [[Casterwill family]]) or evil factions ([[the Organization]] and [[Blood Spiral]]). Each player also may construct a Legendary Hero pile as a side deck to hold Legendary Heroes without counting towards the 40-card maximum.
*One player (the "lead player") chooses a Mission card. A Mission card informs the players how to set up the Map (the game board), as well as the conditions of victory. 
*Both players then take turns back and forth while proceeding through seven rounds. The lead player seeks to complete the victory conditions of his or her Mission card, while his or her opponent (the "defending player") attempts to prevent this until the end of the seventh round.
*If the lead player completes the Mission within the time limit, he or she wins the game. If seven rounds elapse and the lead player hasn't won, the defending player is then the victor.
*Once a hero card is played, it may either be moved around the map, use a special power, begin a fight, or go after a Mission goal. Upon using the card's allotted action per turn, the card is exhausted for the turn and turned sideways. Additionally, some card abilities are able to exhaust a hero, rendering the target unable to use its allotted action for the turn.

Hero Type — Description — Key Rules
Major Hero — Powerful or influential heroes that form the core of a player’s strategy. — Limited to one per round. Counts toward the Major Hero limit even if played by card effects.

sections.heading: Zones
sections.wikitext: Zones on the Mission Map are separated into numbers (1 - 5), with 1 being the closest to a player and 5 being the farthest. The opponent's zones share the same spaces but are numbered in the reverse order. If a card is played that mentions a zone number, the zone number of the card's player is used.  When the lead player is setting up a [[:Category:Mission cards|Mission]], his or her zone numbers are used to place the Mission features.

sections.heading: TCG Terms
sections.wikitext:
''For a full list of terms, see the [[Huntik Trading Card Game/Glossary|Huntik TCG Glossary]]''
* ATK - Short for attack, the representation of a hero's combat prowess.
* DEF - Short for defense, the representation of a hero's protection level.
* KO - Short for knocked out, the state in which a hero is unusable in the game.
* Unblockable - A hero cannot be prevented from moving by an opponent's being in a zone.
* Forceful - Attacks a hero adds to a combat cannot be removed.

• Both players then take turns back and forth while proceeding through seven rounds. The lead player seeks to complete the victory conditions of his or her Mission card, while his or her opponent (the "defending player") attempts to prevent this until the end of the seventh round.
• If the lead player completes the Mission within the time limit, he or she wins the game. If seven rounds elapse and the lead player hasn't won, the defending player is then the victor.
• Once a hero card is played, it may either be moved around the map, use a special power, begin a fight, or go after a Mission goal. Upon using the card's allotted action per turn, the card is exhausted for the turn and turned sideways. Additionally, some card abilities are able to exhaust a hero, rendering the target unable to use its allotted action for the turn.

Types of Cards

The Huntik Trading Card Game features several distinct card types, each serving a specific role within gameplay.

Hero Cards

Hero cards represent Seekers and Titans. Heroes are placed on the Mission Map and are the primary way players interact with the game and move around the Mission Map.

Hero Type — Description — Key Rules
Major Hero — Powerful or influential heroes that form the core of a player’s strategy. — Limited to one per round. Counts toward the Major Hero limit even if played by card effects.
Minor Hero — Supporting heroes with specialized abilities. — No limit on how many may be played per round.
Legendary Hero — The Legendary Titans and the most powerful Hero cards in the game. — Played using matching Amulet cards; Placed in the Legendary Hero pile and not shuffled into the deck. Counts as the Major Hero for the round. Returns to the Legendary pile when KO’d.
Action Cards

Action cards represent spells, abilities, tactics, and special maneuvers used during the game.

Action Type — Description — Turn Cost
Exhaust Action — Focused or powerful effects channeled through a Hero. — Requires exhausting a ready Hero and consumes the player’s turn.
Free Action — Quick tactics or effects that do not require a Hero. — Consumes the player’s turn but does not require exhausting a Hero.
Combat Action — Tactical reactions played during combat. — Does not consume the player’s turn; played only during combat.
Mission Cards

Mission cards define the objective of the game and determine how victory is achieved. Many missions are based off the Huntik team's missions in the TV series.

Mission Type — Description — Notes
Training Mission — Introductory missions designed to teach the rules. — Not legal in official tournament play.
Expert Mission — Advanced missions with more complex objectives. — Intended for competitive play.
Mutual Mission — Missions that either player may complete. — May result in a draw if unresolved.
Solo Mission — Missions designed for single-player gameplay. — Designed for single-player use with automated rules.
Zones

Zones on the Mission Map are separated into numbers (1 - 5), with 1 being the closest to a player and 5 being the farthest. The opponent's zones share the same spaces but are numbered in the reverse order. If a card is played that mentions a zone number, the zone number of the card's player is used. When the lead player is setting up a Mission, his or her zone numbers are used to place the Mission features.

TCG Terms

For a full list of terms, see the Huntik TCG Glossary
• ATK - Short for attack, the representation of a hero's combat prowess.
• DEF - Short for defense, the representation of a hero's protection level.
• KO - Short for knocked out, the state in which a hero is unusable in the game.
• Unblockable - A hero cannot be prevented from moving by an opponent's being in a zone.
• Forceful - Attacks a hero adds to a combat cannot be removed.

Card Rarity

There are different rarities of cards in the TCG, with some cards being much rarer than others. There are often certain identifiers that determine the rarity of a card. The ratio represents the chances of finding the specific rarity in a booster pack.

Rarity — Notes — Ratio
Common — Standard card, no visual effects — 8:1
Rare — Holofoil artwork — 1:1
Mission/Feature — Card labelled Mission or Feature — 1:3
Super Rare — Holofoil artwork, ATK/DEF numbers, borders — 1:9
Ultra Rare — Holofoil entirety, embossed with Icons, Legendary Heroes — 1:21
Exclusive — Only available through tournaments/special purchases — N/A
Trivia

• The Huntik TCG is notable for featuring numerous original characters and Titans. One Titan, Enfluxion, originally designed for the TCG, would go on to appear in Season 2 of the television series with an overhauled design.

Sources

• Information on the game can be found at Huntik.com

Big Bocca |artwork = Cold Fuzion Studios |publisher = [[Upper Deck]] |release date = February 17, 2009 |genre = Collectible card game}} The '''Huntik Trading Card Game''' (TCG) is a two-player trading card game based upon the ''[[Huntik: Secrets & Seekers]]'' television series. The cards, which are collected randomly by players and assembled into 40-card decks, represent various [[Seekers]], [[Titans]], and [[spells]] from the world of Huntik. The game was published by [[Upper Deck]] Entertainment in Europe and the United States and launched on February 17, 2009 with the release of the [[TCG:Secrets and Seekers|Secrets and Seekers]] [[TCG:Starter Deck|Starter Deck]] and its supporting boosters. It was accompanied by the [[Huntik TCG Tutorial]], a special minisode featuring [[Lok Lambert]], [[Dante Vale]] and [[Cherit]] playing and explaining the game. Each Huntik booster pack contains 9 cards, including a foil rare in every pack while 1 in every 3 contains a password card that could unlock exclusive content on [[Huntik.com]]. The Huntik TCG is notable for its integration into the ''Huntik'' television series, with the visual design of the cards closely resembling the informational cards displayed on the [[Holotome]] in the series, and the Titan cards functioning as an in-universe extension of the Holotome's Titan profile system, translating on-screen information into a playable format. March 30, 2010 (cancelled) |- | colspan="4" style="padding:0.4em 0.4em;" | This unreleased expansion set would have featured a brand new starter deck containing six exclusive foils and would have introuduced a new [[Seeker]] faction, the Krono Relic Hunters. |} == History == ===Development and Launch=== Big Bocca's development of the Huntik TCG began in 2008, designing its mechanics alongside the production of the ''Huntik'' television series, ensuring close thematic integration between the cards and the show’s characters, Titans, locations, and story arcs. It was particularly notable for expanding on Huntik's mythology, introducing many original [[Seekers]], [[Titans]] and [[Spells]] and providing new information and backstories for elements in the show. Ahead of the TCG's official launch, Sneak Preview events were organised by Upper Deck where exclusive [[TCG:Pre-Release Cards|Pre-Release Cards]] were given out. The first set, [[TCG:Secrets and Seekers|Secrets and Seekers]], was released on February 17, 2009. It introduced the core gameplay mechanics, and featured characters and Titan from first half of the [[Season 1|first season]] of the show and consisted of the [[TCG:Starter Deck|Starter Deck]] and booster packs. A special [[Huntik TCG Tutorial]] was also released featuring [[Lok Lambert]], [[Dante Vale]] and [[Cherit]] playing the game and explaining the gameplay to the viewers. Later in 2009, Upper Deck released two expansion sets: [[TCG:Legendary Saga|Legendary Saga]] (June 2009), which introduced the four Legendary Titans and added higher-rarity, more powerful hero cards, and [[TCG:Omens and Legacies|Omens and Legacies]] (October 2009), which expanded the game’s narrative scope by introducing new factions such as the [[Blood Spiral|Blood Spirals]] and incorporating elements from later parts of the series’ storyline. In addition to standard expansions, Upper Deck released [[TCG:Promotional Cards|Promotional Cards]] through organized play programs such as Seeker League events and tournaments, as well as special collector products like the [[TCG:Huntik Holotome Tin|Huntik Holotome Tin]], which bundled booster packs with exclusive cards. === Planned Expansions and Cancellation === Upper Deck had planned to continue supporting the Huntik TCG with additional expansions in 2010, notably the fourth set, [[TCG:Labyrinth of Doom|Labyrinth of Doom]], which was intended to further develop the game’s mechanics and story content and feature characters from the show's [[Season 2|second season]]. However, this set was never released due to Upper Deck Entertainment filing for bankruptcy amid legal disputes and financial difficulties. As a result, production and organized support for several of the company’s trading card games including the Huntik TCG were discontinued.
